newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--Just 20 days after its swearing-in ceremony, the new government is already providing indications of tension and clashes within its ranks. In the economic team, junior ministers appear to be opposing National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou on crucial issues such as the taxation of state titles and real estate holdings.
--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos adds his personal opinion that the taxation of bonds and treasury bills would be a "just act".

--Jostling for position in New Democracy: Tension in the main opposition party continues as failed leadership candidate George Souflias appears determined to continue his push for the leadership and president Miltiades Evert begins talks ahead of tomorrow's expected announcement of changes to key party positions.

--Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis puts question mark over application of new national high school certificate, increasing possibility of clash with his predecessor George Papandreou, now holding the alternate foreign minister post.
--Brussels reaction to murder of unarmed Greek Cypriot in Cyprus on Sunday "muted". Nicosia has not yet ruled out protesting to the United Nations.
--Positive developments in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia (FYROM) issue as a new round of talks is decided, under the aegis of UN mediator Cyrus Vance.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA

--Despite government denials, government members appear to be in favour of the taxing of state titles. National Economy Deputy Minister Alekos Baltas's comments in favour greeted by trade unions, Communist Party and Left Coalition.
--Government continues to fend off criticism of appointment of Sunday newspaper 'To Vima' publisher Stavros Psyharis to post of governor of autonomous monastic community Mount Athos.
Government spokesman Dimitris Reppas says the decision is final: "Nobody asked us", say communities on Mount Athos.
TA NEA
--Insurance firms demand 30 percent increase on car insurance premiums to offset losses of past year.
--MPs react to moves by Parliament Speaker Apostolos Kaklamanis to institute roll-calls and penalties for absent MPs. MPs prepare petition to bring issue to Parliament.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--The state sells off its real estate. Some 45,000 properties go under the hammer for quick cash to plug the 'black hole' in the budget.
--More than 300,000 property owners face face fines of up to 500,000 drachmas for failing to submit declarations of ownership.
ETHNOS

--Tax collectors begin their tax 'frenzy' this week to collect the 150 billion drachmas needed. Plans will be firmed at tomorrow's meeting of Economy Deputy Minister George Drys with officials of special tax collection department and tax department.

--Foreign Minister Pangalos castigates Turkish orders to shoot to kill anyone approaching the dividing line on Cyprus, as part of Ankara's efforts to scuttle any attempt at resolving the Cyprus issue.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis chairs meeting on changes to National Health System (ESY). Officials to examine unification of all health sectors as well as reappraisal of disability benefits.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
